def.short: the way your body, face and hands show your feelings without words
def.long: The way the position and movements of your body, face and hands show what you feel or think, often without you knowing it.

grammar.pattern: sb's body language; read body language

examples.en: His body language said he was nervous.
examples.tr: Beden dili gergin olduğunu gösteriyordu.

examples.en: In interviews, good body language is as important as good answers.
examples.tr: Mülakatlarda iyi bir beden dili, iyi cevaplar kadar önemlidir.

examples.en: She said she was fine, but her body language told a different story.
examples.tr: İyi olduğunu söyledi ama beden dili başka bir şey anlatıyordu.

tr.note: Kollarını kavuşturmak, gözünü kaçırmak ya da gülümsemek beden dilinin örnekleridir.

quiz.cloze: He said he wasn't angry, but his ______ showed something else: crossed arms and a red face.

entries.sense_note: looking at someone's eyes while talking

def.short: looking straight into someone's eyes while you talk or listen to them
def.long: When two people look at each other's eyes at the same time. In many cultures it shows that you are honest and listening.

examples.en: Make eye contact when you speak.
examples.tr: Konuşurken göz teması kur.

examples.en: He was so shy that he avoided eye contact with everyone.
examples.tr: O kadar utangaçtı ki herkesle göz temasından kaçınıyordu.

examples.en: Good eye contact helps you look confident in a job interview.
examples.tr: İyi göz teması, iş görüşmesinde kendinden emin görünmene yardımcı olur.

tr.note: 'Make eye contact' (göz teması kurmak) ve 'avoid eye contact' (göz temasından kaçınmak) kalıpları yaygındır.

quiz.cloze: He was nervous and avoided ______ with the interviewer the whole time.

def.short: something you say or write to show you are sorry for doing something wrong
def.long: Words you say or write to tell someone that you are sorry because you hurt them or did something wrong.

grammar.pattern: an apology for sth; owe sb an apology

examples.en: I owe you an apology.
examples.tr: Sana bir özür borçluyum.

examples.en: She accepted his apology and they shook hands.
examples.tr: Onun özrünü kabul etti ve el sıkıştılar.

examples.en: The airline sent all passengers an apology for the delay.
examples.tr: Havayolu şirketi gecikme için bütün yolculara bir özür mesajı gönderdi.

tr.note: Fiil hâli 'apologize' olur ve kişi 'to' ile gelir: 'I apologize to you' ('from you' değil). Kibar bir kalıp: 'Please accept my apologies.'

quiz.cloze: I'm still waiting for his ______, but he keeps saying it wasn't his fault.

def.short: comments that say what is bad or wrong about someone or something
def.long: Comments or opinions that show what is bad or wrong with a person, their work or an idea. Useful comments that help you get better are called 'constructive'.

examples.en: He doesn't take criticism well.
examples.tr: Eleştiriyi kaldıramaz.

examples.en: The new law faced strong criticism from teachers.
examples.tr: Yeni yasa öğretmenlerden sert eleştiri aldı.

examples.en: Your criticism helped me improve my report.
examples.tr: Eleştirin raporumu geliştirmeme yardımcı oldu.

tr.note: Türkçede eleştiriye bazen 'kritik' denir ama İngilizce 'critic' eleştirmen demektir. Eleştirinin kendisi 'criticism' olur.

mistakes.wrong: I don't like his critics about my work.
mistakes.right: I don't like his criticism of my work.
mistakes.why: Türkçede eleştiriye 'kritik' de denir, bu yüzden 'critic' seçilir. Ama 'critic' eleştirmen demektir; eleştirinin kendisi 'criticism' olur.

quiz.cloze: The manager's ______ was harsh, but it helped me do a better job.

entries.sense_note: words that say someone did well

def.micro: words that say you did well
def.short: words that show you admire someone or think they did something well
def.long: Words that show you think someone has done something very well or that you admire them. Teachers, parents and managers use them to encourage people.

grammar.pattern: praise for sb/sth; words of praise

examples.en: The new film got a lot of praise.
examples.tr: Yeni film çok övgü aldı.

examples.en: A little praise can make children work harder.
examples.tr: Biraz övgü, çocukların daha çok çalışmasını sağlayabilir.

examples.en: The firefighters received praise from the mayor for their quick work.
examples.tr: İtfaiyeciler hızlı çalışmaları için belediye başkanından övgü aldı.

tr.note: Sayılamaz bir isimdir: 'a praise' denmez, 'a lot of praise' ya da 'words of praise' denir. Fiil olarak da kullanılır: 'praise someone'.

mistakes.wrong: She got a big praise from her boss.
mistakes.right: She got a lot of praise from her boss.
mistakes.why: Türkçede 'büyük bir övgü aldı' denir ve 'bir' 'a' diye çevrilir. İngilizcede 'praise' sayılamaz, 'a' almaz.

quiz.cloze: Her teacher's ______ made her feel proud of all her hard work.

def.short: the opinion or feeling you get about someone or something, often quickly
def.long: The opinion or feeling you have about someone or something, often after meeting or seeing them for the first time. The first one is often hard to change.

grammar.pattern: make an impression on sb; first impression

examples.en: You only get one chance to make a first impression.
examples.tr: İlk izlenim bırakmak için tek bir şansın var.

examples.en: My first impression of Ankara was very good.
examples.tr: Ankara hakkındaki ilk izlenimim çok iyiydi.

examples.en: Burak made a great impression on his new boss.
examples.tr: Burak yeni patronu üzerinde harika bir izlenim bıraktı.

tr.note: Kalıplar: 'make an impression on someone' (birinde izlenim bırakmak), 'I got the impression that…' (… gibi bir izlenime kapıldım).

quiz.cloze: She made a good first ______ at the interview by arriving early and smiling.

entries.sense_note: what you do or feel in response

def.short: what you say, feel or do because of something that has happened
def.long: What you say, feel or do as an answer to something that happens or something someone says. It can be quick, like a laugh, or slow, like a decision.

grammar.pattern: a reaction to sth; sb's first reaction

examples.en: What was his reaction to the news?
examples.tr: Habere tepkisi ne oldu?

examples.en: Her first reaction was to laugh.
examples.tr: İlk tepkisi gülmek oldu.

examples.en: The public's reaction to the new tax was very negative.
examples.tr: Halkın yeni vergiye tepkisi çok olumsuzdu.

tr.note: 'Reaction to something' kalıbıyla kullanılır. Fiil hâli 'react' (tepki vermek) olur.

quiz.cloze: When I told him I was moving abroad, his first ______ was silence.

def.short: words or actions that give someone confidence or hope to do something
def.long: Words or support that make someone feel more confident and more ready to try something or to keep going.

grammar.pattern: encouragement from sb; words of encouragement

examples.en: Thanks for your encouragement.
examples.tr: Bana cesaret verdiğin için teşekkürler.

examples.en: With a little encouragement, Deniz started singing in public.
examples.tr: Biraz cesaretlendirilince Deniz herkesin önünde şarkı söylemeye başladı.

examples.en: The coach shouted words of encouragement from the side of the field.
examples.tr: Antrenör sahanın kenarından cesaret verici sözler bağırdı.

tr.note: Sayılamaz bir isimdir. Fiil hâli 'encourage' (cesaretlendirmek, teşvik etmek) olur.

quiz.cloze: The crowd's loud ______ helped the tired runner reach the finish line.

entries.sense_note: story that may not be true

def.micro: story that may not be true
def.short: a piece of news that people tell each other, which may or may not be true
def.long: Information that people pass from person to person, but nobody knows if it is true. Stories like this spread quickly at work, at school or online.

grammar.pattern: a rumor that…; a rumor about sth

examples.en: There's a rumor that the boss is leaving.
examples.tr: Patronun ayrılacağına dair bir söylenti var.

examples.en: Don't believe every rumor you hear online.
examples.tr: İnternette duyduğun her söylentiye inanma.

examples.en: The rumor about the factory closing turned out to be false.
examples.tr: Fabrikanın kapanacağı söylentisi asılsız çıktı.

tr.note: İngiliz yazımı 'rumour' olur. 'Gossip' daha çok insanların özel hayatı hakkındaki dedikodudur; 'rumor' doğruluğu belli olmayan haberdir.

quiz.cloze: There's a ______ going around the office that we'll all get a bonus this year.

def.short: a situation in which people have different opinions about something
def.long: A situation in which people do not have the same opinion about something, sometimes with a small argument.

grammar.pattern: a disagreement about sth; a disagreement with sb

examples.en: We had a small disagreement about money.
examples.tr: Para konusunda küçük bir anlaşmazlık yaşadık.

examples.en: There is some disagreement among doctors about this treatment.
examples.tr: Bu tedavi konusunda doktorlar arasında bazı görüş ayrılıkları var.

examples.en: After a disagreement with her manager, Zeynep asked to move to another team.
examples.tr: Müdürüyle bir anlaşmazlık yaşadıktan sonra Zeynep başka bir ekibe geçmek istedi.

tr.note: 'Conflict' daha ciddi bir anlaşmazlıktır. 'Disagreement' yalnızca fikir ayrılığı da olabilir, kavga olması gerekmez.

quiz.cloze: There was some ______ between the doctors: two wanted surgery and one did not.

def.short: the quality of being friendly, generous and caring towards other people
def.long: Being friendly, generous and caring towards other people, for example helping someone without wanting anything back.

grammar.pattern: an act of kindness; show kindness to sb

examples.en: A small act of kindness can change someone's day.
examples.tr: Küçük bir iyilik birinin gününü değiştirebilir.

examples.en: I'll never forget the kindness of our neighbors when we moved here.
examples.tr: Buraya taşındığımızda komşularımızın gösterdiği iyiliği hiç unutmayacağım.

examples.en: Treat animals with kindness.
examples.tr: Hayvanlara şefkatle davranın.

tr.note: Birinden iyilik isterken 'Can you do me a favor?' denir; bu kalıpta 'kindness' kullanılmaz.

quiz.cloze: It was an act of real ______ when the stranger paid for the old man's bus ticket.

def.micro: a bad quality or weak point
def.short: a part of someone's character or skills that is not good enough
def.long: A part of your character, skills or work that is not as good as the rest. In job interviews people often ask about your strengths and these.

grammar.pattern: strengths and weaknesses; a weakness for sth

examples.en: Everyone has strengths and weaknesses.
examples.tr: Herkesin güçlü ve zayıf yönleri vardır.

examples.en: My biggest weakness is that I talk too much.
examples.tr: En büyük zayıf yönüm çok konuşmam.

examples.en: In the interview, Can talked honestly about his weaknesses.
examples.tr: Mülakatta Can zayıf yönlerinden dürüstçe bahsetti.

tr.note: 'Have a weakness for something' bir şeye karşı zaafın olması demektir: 'I have a weakness for chocolate.'

quiz.cloze: In the interview, they asked me about my strengths and ______.
